text:
sana: FYI — seeing ~0.2% 503s from our ALB in us-west-2. Its narrowly concentrated to traffic that egresses through a couple of corporate NAT IPs.

devon: Can you paste an access log line and an example client IP so we can trace NAT and ASNs?

sana: Pasted a redacted ALB access entry in case it helps:
```
https 2026-03-18T15:04:12.123Z app/my-alb/abcd0123 10.0.4.5:54321 10.0.6.7:443 0.001 0.001 0.000 503 503 0 57 GET https://api.prod.redwood.ai/health HTTP/1.1 curl/7.79.1 - - arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:.. - - - TLSv1.3 ECDHE_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 - - - -
```
Note the SNI field is "-" for the failing lines.

ben: If SNI is missing ALB falls back to default cert/listener rule. That can route to a maintenance/503 target group depending on rule ordering. Do logs show sni == "-" only for the bad IPs?

sana: Yes, good correlation. For other IPs the sni value is the hostname as expected. I grabbed a packet capture behind one of the reported NATs and the ClientHello truly lacks the server_name extension.

alix: That points to TLS inspection middleboxes (stripping SNI) or older clients. Another possibility is ECH being used by the client so the outer ClientHello doesn't carry a readable sni. ALB cannot see inner ECH-hostname.

devon: Repro steps I ran: from our dev host `openssl s_client -connect api.prod.redwood.ai:443 -tlsextdebug -status` shows Server Name present and cert chain ok. From a VM inside the corp NAT the ClientHello shows no server_name but the TCP/TLS handshake still completes. So something on that egress path alters the ClientHello.

paul: Short-term mitigation options:
- Add the affected hostnames as SANs to the default edge cert so clients that send no SNI still get a cert that matches.
- Add a fallback listener rule that maps default cert to primary TG (low-risk).
- Consider moving sensitive routes to TCP passthrough (NLB) so backend can terminate TLS or handle ECH.

ben: I recommend the SAN add as a fast safety net while we investigate the middlebox. Also we should build monitoring for sni=="-" so this is visible by ASN/IP.

alix: Agreed. Follow-ups:
- alert when pct(sni=="-") > 0.1% for 10m
- dashboard top ASNs/IPs with missing SNI
- region breakdown (so far only us-west-2)

sana: I created PR #4321 to add the few impacted hostnames to the default wildcard cert (staging validation now).

ingress-bot: deploy started for ingress-config v2026-03-18-2312 by sana (canary 1/10 hosts)

devon: Note: ECH clients will still be a problem because ALB cannot read encrypted inner SNI. For long-term we should evaluate fronting options that support ECH or a TLS passthrough path for customers behind corporate proxies.

ben: I'll add metrics and an alert for sni-missing grouped by client ASN/IP and wire up a dashboard card.

alix: After the PR: watch for regressions and plan a postmortem if we see recurrence. Also open a ticket with partners/security asking if any TLS inspection or ECH policy rolled out on their NATs recently.

sana: Canary finished: canary 1/10 reported no 503s from the traced IPs. Promoting after 1h watch.

deploy-bot: Release v2026-03-18-2312 promoted to prod (sana) — started at 2026-03-18T15:36:20Z

paul: Please post ALB access log counts for sni=="-" after the hour so we can confirm the drop. If stable, create follow-up for longer-term ECH handling and add guidance to runbooks.

ben: Created dashboards and linked them in #eng-infra-dashboards. Added a short-term fallback rule experiment to see if that further reduces noise.

sana: Closing thread for now  will reopen if we see recurrence. Thanks all :thumbsup:
